chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī, who said:

I was with Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام after his son Abū Jaʿfar had passed away, and I was thinking to myself, wanting to say: It is as though these two—I mean Abū Jaʿfar and Abū Muḥammad—at this time are like Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā and Ismāʿīl, the two sons of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, and that their story is like their story, as Abū Muḥammad was the one anticipated after Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام.

So Abū al-Ḥasan turned toward me before I spoke and said: Yes, O Abū Hāshim, there occurred for Allah regarding Abū Muḥammad after Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that which had not been known for him, just as there occurred for Him regarding Mūsā after the passing of Ismāʿīl that by which his condition was disclosed. And it is just as your soul told you, even if the falsifiers dislike it. And Abū Muḥammad, my son, is the successor after me; with him is the knowledge of what is needed, and with him is the instrument of the Imamate.

key_terms.آلَةُ الْإِمَامَةِ: the means or qualifying marks of the Imamate
key_terms.الْمُبْطِلُونَ: those who uphold falsehood or seek to invalidate the truth
key_terms.الْمُرْجَأَ: the one expected or deferred for a later role
key_terms.بَدَا: there occurred a manifesting or disclosure in the divine matter
key_terms.عِلْمُ مَا يُحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ: the knowledge required for the community’s needs

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the Imamate of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام after Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts Abū Hāshim al-Jaʿfarī’s inner reflection after the death of Abū Jaʿfar and the response of Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام before he even spoke. The Imam عليه السلام affirms the succession of Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام after him, drawing a parallel with the earlier case of Mūsā and Ismāʿīl, and states that Abū Muḥammad possesses the needed knowledge and the marks of the Imamate.
